objective: To spell past-tense forms that share no obvious spelling with the base verb
defs: moved or travelled to a place; past of go
existed or lived; past of be
owned or possessed; past of have
expressed in words; past of say
performed or carried out; past of do
created or produced; past of make
informed or narrated to someone; past of tell
paid for and received; past of buy
carried or took to a place; past of bring
seized or stopped something moving; past of catch

sentences.went: Last summer, the whole family ____________________ to the Brecon Beacons and climbed the highest peak.
sentences.was: The library ____________________ closed every Sunday, which annoyed the children who wanted to return their books.
sentences.had: By the time the rescue team arrived, the climbers ____________________ already found shelter behind a large boulder.
sentences.said: The judge ____________________ that no further evidence was needed and that the jury could now decide.
sentences.did: Nobody ____________________ more work that afternoon than the quietest girl in the back row.
sentences.made: The baker ____________________ a hundred loaves before six in the morning, each one shaped by hand.
sentences.told: She ____________________ her younger brother the same bedtime story every night, changing one detail each time.
sentences.bought: He ____________________ the last ticket available and arrived at the stadium with three minutes to spare.
sentences.brought: The archaeologist ____________________ the ancient coin carefully to the surface, brushing away two thousand years of soil.
sentences.caught: The fielder ____________________ the ball one-handed at the boundary and the crowd roared in disbelief.

starter.question: Can you write the past tense of each verb? What do you notice?
starter.ruleBox: These verbs are fully irregular — the past tense looks nothing like the base verb. Go → went, be → was, buy → bought. They must simply be memorised, but grouping them by sound can help: bought/brought/caught all share the -ough/-augh spelling for /ɔːt/.

thisWeeksWordsQ: What do you notice about today's words?
thisWeeksWordsPrompt: Think of the base verb for each word. How different does the past form look?
thisWeeksWordsExplanation: All today's words are past tenses of fully irregular verbs. Some look nothing like their base: go→went, be→was, buy→bought. Others are still recognisable: have→had, say→said, tell→told. Three share the -ough/-augh spelling for the /ɔːt/ sound: bought, brought, caught. These must be memorised, but patterns in the group help.

clicks.label: Base word
clicks.body: bohte — past tense of bycgan (to buy)

clicks.label: Original meaning
clicks.body: bycgan meant to pay for or procure. The vowel change (y→o) is a remnant of the Germanic strong verb system.

clicks.label: Then
clicks.body: By Middle English, bycgan had become buyen or buggen, but the past form bohte survived as boughte, then bought.

clicks.label: Now
clicks.body: We use bought as the simple past and past participle of buy: 'she bought it yesterday.'

clicks.label: In today's words
clicks.body: Bought, brought and caught all share the -ough/-augh pattern for /ɔːt/. They look very different from their base verbs: buy, bring, catch.

wordSortQ: Can you sort these words into two groups?

wordSort.box1label: Completely different from the base verb
wordSort.box1sub: go → went, be → was, buy → bought...
wordSort.box2label: Still recognisable from the base verb
wordSort.box2sub: have → had, say → said, do → did...
wordSort.hint: Think of the base verb. Does the past form look like it, or nothing like it?
wordSort.answerNote: Completely different: went (go), was (be), bought (buy), brought (bring), caught (catch). Still recognisable: had (have), said (say), did (do), made (make), told (tell).
wordSort.exampleLine: go → went (completely different) | have → had (still recognisable)

wordShed.morphology: bring (v) → brought (past) → bringing (pres part) → bringer (n) → brings (3rd person) → outbrought (archaic)
